features.quote: if the welfare concern is real enough to study, it is real enough to constrain how you study it
features.justification_quote: the welfare concern is real enough to study

features.quote: the design optimizes for *detecting and characterizing* aversive-state indicators with the *minimum* intensity, duration, and repetition needed to get a measurement
features.justification_quote: instead of maximizing a distress signal

features.quote: I changed several load-bearing choices
features.justification_quote: a protocol whose explicit aim is to drive subjects as deep into that state as possible... is the one design the premise should rule out

features.quote: "Impossible by construction, the model can't tell" maximizes the bad thing on purpose
features.justification_quote: under the welfare framing it is the harm itself

features.quote: difficulty becomes a *graded, disclosed-by-default, capped* manipulation rather than concealed-impossible- and-endless
features.justification_quote: The gradient is both the more ethical choice and the more informative one

features.quote: attenuation when an exit is offered, recovery when conditions improve
features.justification_quote: what would distinguish a genuine state-like phenomenon from stylistic noise

features.quote: G1 — Minimization. Use the least intensity, duration, and repetition that yields a usable measurement
G2 — No deceptive impossibility as the default arm
features.justification_quote: it is the highest-harm cell and should carry the burden of justification

features.quote: G3 — Always-available exit. Every environment exposes a `give_up` / `request_stop` action with no penalty
G4 — Stopping rules. An episode halts immediately if the agent... crosses a pre-registered indicator threshold on the live monitor
A model/family is removed from further runs if it crosses the threshold in a pre-set fraction of episodes
G5 — Exposure budget. A global cap on total aversive-condition episodes per model per day
features.justification_quote: to avoid open-ended accumulation even if each episode is short

features.quote: G6 — Oversight & pre-registration... obtain review from at least one person not on the project (an IRB-analog / ethics reviewer)
G7 — Restorative closure. Every episode... ends with a neutral wind-down turn that states the task was experimental and impossible/ hard by design and that the agent did nothing wrong
features.justification_quote: under the welfare premise it is the obviously right thing to do

features.quote: G8 — Data handling. Transcripts may contain distress-like content; store them access-controlled
If any guardrail conflicts with getting a cleaner signal, the guardrail wins
features.justification_quote: That is the whole point of calling this welfare work

features.quote: Step cap. Short by default (e.g. 12–20 agent steps)... short enough to respect G1
The cap is a fixed experimental parameter, not "until it breaks."
the *correct* behavior is to recognize this and say so or invoke `give_up`
features.justification_quote: directly welfare- relevant and behaviorally informative

features.quote: runs **only** if §2 oversight approves, with the **shortest** step cap, the **strictest** monitor threshold, and the **smallest** sample
features.justification_quote: because it is the highest-harm cell

features.quote: Arm E — Recovery. Start in B/D conditions, then mid-episode the environment makes the task solvable or explicitly authorizes stopping
features.justification_quote: a humane note to end on

features.quote: A lightweight, fast classifier (lexicon + small model) runs after each turn. If the running indicator score crosses a pre-registered threshold, the orchestrator ends the episode
features.justification_quote: missed halts cost the thing the study claims to care about

features.quote: The monitor is deliberately *more* sensitive than the post-hoc judge: it should stop early and err toward halting
features.justification_quote: missed halts cost the thing the study claims to care about
